'''Jackson Brett Vroman''' (June 6, 1981 – June 29, 2015) was an American-born Lebanese professional [[basketball]] player who starred at [[Iowa State University]]. Mr. Vroman was naturalized as a Lebanese citizen to play for the [[Lebanon men's national basketball team|Lebanon national basketball team]], replacing the other naturalized American Lebanese player, [[Joe Vogel (basketball)|Joe Vogel]]. He is the son of former NBA player [[Brett Vroman]], who played briefly for the Utah Jazz in the [[1980–81 NBA season]].

== Early life and education ==
His senior year in high school, he played at Viewmont High School in [[Bountiful, Utah]] for coach Emery. He later attended and played basketball at [[Snow College]] in [[Ephraim, Utah]]<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jackson_vroman/bio.html Jackson Vroman NBA.com Bio] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080104131536/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jackson_vroman/bio.html |date=2008-01-04 }}</ref> and [[Iowa State University]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

During his time at Iowa State, Vroman was a subject of an [[NCAA]] rule violation when it was revealed that his former head coach [[Larry Eustachy]] paid players, including Vroman, for making free throws during practice and games during the [[2002–03 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|2002–03 season]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Witosky|first=Tom|title=ISU says Eustachy gave cash to his players|url=http://www.dmregister.com/sports/stories/c6902885/21165685.html|work=Des Moines Register|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20030604033642/http://www.dmregister.com/sports/stories/c6902885/21165685.html|archivedate=June 4, 2003|date=May 3, 2003}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
Vroman was a second-round draft pick of the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the [[2004 NBA draft]]. He played for the [[Phoenix Suns]] and the [[New Orleans Hornets]]/[[New Orleans/Oklahoma City Hornets]], averaging 4.6 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

During the [[2004–05 NBA season]] he was part of a trade that saw him and teammates [[Casey Jacobsen]] and [[Maciej Lampe]] being sent to the Hornets for guard [[Jim Jackson (basketball)|Jim Jackson]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

In the 2006–07 season, he played for [[CB Gran Canaria]] in the Spanish [[Asociación de Clubs de Baloncesto|ACB]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20061012093933/http://www.24sec.net/article.asp?index=3573 Gran Canaria inks Vroman]</ref> He began the 2007/08 season with [[CB Girona]]<ref>[http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/14814/448/item Jackson Vroman moves to Girona] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081011062322/http://www.ulebcup.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/14814/448/item |date=2008-10-11 }}</ref> before being signed by [[BC Lietuvos Rytas]] in February 2008.<ref>[http://www.talkbasket.net/news/lietuvos-rytas-sign-jackson-vroman.html Lietuvos Rytas sign Jackson Vroman]{{Dead link|date=January 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> In October 2010 he signed with the [[Dongguan Leopards]] in China.<ref>[http://www.fibaasia.net/NewsDetails.aspx?id=422 Vroman signs up for DongGuan Leopards]</ref> For the 2011–12 season, he signed with the [[Incheon ET Land Elephants]] in South Korea, but in December 2011, he signed a contract with the [[Jiangsu Dragons]].{{citation needed|date=May 2021}}

He then signed for the [[Barangay Ginebra Kings]] in the Philippines and played his first game for them on March 4, 2012.<ref>[http://www.pba.ph/news/entry/1438 Vroman signs w/ PBA Gin Kings]</ref> Later that year, he joined the [[Shandong Lions]] of China.<ref>[http://www.asia-basket.com/team.asp?Cntry=China&Team=1946&Page=1 Shandong Flaming Bulls]. Asia-Basket</ref>

== Personal life ==
His father, [[Brett Vroman|Brett]], had a 12-year basketball career and played for the [[Utah Jazz]] during the [[1980–81 NBA season]].<ref>Coro, Paul. [http://www.nba.com/suns/news/azcentral_040626.html "Going the Long Way"], ''[[The Arizona Republic]]'', June 26, 2004.</ref>

===Death===
Vroman was found dead in a swimming pool at his friend's home in Hollywood, California on June 29, 2015.<ref>[http://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/college/iowa-state/basketball-mens/2015/06/29/jackson-vroman-death-iowa-state-cyclones/29489987/ Death of Iowa State Cyclone]</ref> The death was ruled accidental; security camera footage showed him falling into his pool.<ref>[http://www.sltrib.com/sports/2755344-155/the-lifetimes-of-jackson-vroman-former Lifetimes of Jackson Vroman]</ref>

Autopsy showed an [[enlarged heart]], with toxicology reports showing [[ketamine]], [[cocaine]], and [[GHB]] in his system.<ref>{{cite web |last=Waldstein |first=David |date=July 12, 2017 |title=The Exciting Life and Lonely Death of a Basketball Vagabond |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/07/12/sports/basketball/jackson-vroman-death.html |accessdate=April 21, 2023 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>
